name: Radio
summary: Selects one option from a set.
description: A control for choosing exactly one option from a set, rendered as a button with role="radio" and coordinated by a RadioGroup wrapper that holds the selected value. Each radio shows selected or unselected across the full interaction set — default, hover, focus, active, and disabled — and binds its border, brand inner dot, circular shape, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Choose exactly one option from a small, visible set of choices
Present mutually exclusive options where seeing them all matters
whenNotToUse: Selecting more than one option — use Checkboxes
Choosing from a long list — use a Select to save space

selected.false: Unselected — empty circle with a neutral border.
selected.true: Selected — brand ring with a filled brand inner dot.

states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Wrap radios in a RadioGroup with a clear group label
Give each radio a visible, clickable label
Preselect a sensible default when one clearly applies
donts: Don't use a radio group to allow multiple selections — use Checkboxes
Don't offer a single lone radio — that choice can't be deselected; use a Checkbox
Don't split one logical choice across multiple groups

keyboard: Arrow keys move selection between radios in the group
Tab moves focus into and out of the group as a whole
notes: The group carries role="radiogroup"; each option exposes aria-checked
Only the selected radio (or the first, if none) is in the tab order
Disabled radios are dimmed and skipped
